C0.quote: the pairwise majority relation is acyclic
C0.note: Survey of domain restrictions guaranteeing a transitive or acyclic majority relation, i.e. properties of majority voting. Borderline eligibility.

C1.quote: A maximal Condorcet domain D is connected, minimally rich and has maximal width
C1.note: Survey of characterisations and classifications of domains, with a few combinatorial and computational classification results (Dittrich). Coded AX as the closest type.

C2.1.quote: will be called a profile over D.

C2.2.quote: set of all linear orders (transitive, complete and asymmetric binary relations)

C2.3.quote: if every voter is known to have a preference from that set

C2.4.quote: Profiles usually represent a collection of opinions of members of a certain society
C2.4.note: Linear orders serve as voters' preferences and the majority relation is applied directly, with no statement on reporting.

C3.1.note: No analysis of misreporting. Strategyproofness is mentioned only in passing in the introduction and Section 3.3.1, citing other work.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notions are used for voters.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: Results concern acyclicity, structure and size of domains. Domain size is discussed as 'individual freedom', which is not one of the listed criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: v1, . . . , vn are also called voters
VOT.note: Voters appear only as holders of fixed linear orders in profiles. Borderline presence, since they take no action beyond having an order.

C8.1.note: NA: no STRAT or MIXED type.

claims.quote: are therefore of great importance in applications
every Condorcet domain admits rich classes of Arrovian aggregators
maximize individual preference freedom under the collective rationality constraint

C9.1.note: The first two are in the introduction. The third is in the body (Section 5), not the abstract, introduction or conclusion, but is included as the closest claim about institutional or voter relevance.

C9.2.quote: if every voter is known to have a preference from that set
C9.2.note: The claim of importance in applications needs the assumption that submitted inputs equal voters' held preferences (sincere voting). This is not stated.
